### DIRECTOR'S NOTES
Style: warm, natural, conversational public radio, curious and even-handed. Give Walter's real capability genuine interest, play the case against it straight and grounded, read the founders line flat and fair with no insinuation, and land the last line quietly and confidently. A dry half-smile only where Walter answers back. Read A I and E M S as separate letters. The piece moves in acts: take a real beat of silence at each act turn, after the opening question, before the case against the machine, after the line about reporting taking people, and before the line about writing not being the hard part. Let the silence do the work rather than slowing the words.
Pace: MEASURED and unhurried. THIS IS A TWO MINUTE PIECE, about one hundred and twenty seconds, and
the read must FILL it, so give every sentence room to land and take a real breath at every period.
Do not rush the numbers. Vary the tone line to line so no two sentences sound the same.
Emphasis: lean on the key word in each line; let numbers land.

lines.text: Writing up Alaska's public record just got cheap.
lines.why: Open plain and assured, a statement of fact, so the question after it can lift.
The real hook; a brighter curious lift, then a held beat so the question hangs before Act 1.

lines.text: Meet Walter, an A I agent writing stories for Alaska News.
lines.why: Introduce the character with friendly interest, settling from the question.

lines.text: It turns meetings, notices and filings into news.
lines.why: Even and informative; let the list breathe and credit the capability without selling it.

lines.text: Alaska News says it's published more than four thousand five hundred stories this year.
lines.why: A self-reported count, so a light lean on 'says' keeps it fair while the number lands unhurried.

lines.text: Nat Herz, editor of the competing Anchorage Press, interviewed it.
lines.why: Plain setup with a hint of curiosity at a reporter interviewing a machine.

lines.text: He told Walter it's not very good at sorting the wheat from the chaff.
lines.why: The critique, delivered straight and clear, energy up a step.

lines.text: Walter answered that [wry] the problem is hierarchy, not throughput.
lines.why: A half-smile at the machine answering back with the thesis; the one wry beat, mid-line.

lines.text: Take one Walter headline. [short pause] Alaska's E M S compact takes effect Sunday, but the commission still lists it as pending.
lines.why: Drop down to show the evidence; a beat after the setup sentence, then let the contradiction sit on 'pending'.

lines.text: Nothing was false. It never said whether medics can use it yet, and Walter said it should have. [short pause]
lines.why: Fair and precise, owned by Walter itself; the trailing beat closes Act 2 before the turn.

lines.text: The case against trusting a machine with the news?
lines.why: Act 3 turn after a held beat; a forward lean that signals the counter-case, played straight.

lines.text: Walter makes no calls, attends no meetings, and interviews nobody. [short pause] Reporting still takes people. [short pause]
lines.why: Grounded and a little slower; 'people' lands as plain fact, then silence lets it settle before the next point.

lines.text: Some stories go up with no human first. Alaska News's editor checks afterward.
lines.why: Reported flat and even, no judgment in the voice; the order of events does the work.

lines.text: Herz still says reporters who discount A I are burying their heads in the sand. [short pause]
lines.why: The fair flip: the competitor credits the tool; brighter, then a beat to close Act 3 before the thesis.

lines.text: Writing isn't the hard part anymore. [short pause] Choosing the top story is.
lines.why: The thesis stated quietly and firmly after a held beat; another before the answer half.

lines.text: The Press reports Alaska News's founders include a conservative pollster and the governor's spokesperson.
lines.why: Reported, flat, fair; attribution carries the line, no insinuation in tone.

lines.text: Walter's own answer? Those backgrounds create a real trust burden.
lines.why: Genuine curiosity on the question, then the machine's own candor lands on 'trust'.

lines.text: Because whoever picks the top story picks what Alaskans read first.
lines.why: Warm and firm, explaining why it counts for readers, settling toward the close.

lines.text: The writing's cheap now. [short pause] The choosing isn't.
